title: Dave Reilly, arguing against abolishing business schools — 'good intentions need structural support: ownership, governance and incentives'
summary: An advisor to startups, SMBs and family-owned businesses pushes back on Christopher Marquis's New York Times call to shut down business schools, then concedes the deeper point: the owners he works with take a long view and still get pulled off it. He puts the book forward as the practical answer and would rather business schools taught its principles than closed.
blockquote: He makes the case that good intentions need structural support: ownership, governance and incentives designed to protect a company’s mission through growth and change. It’s a worthwhile read for anyone interested in practical solutions.
attribution_title: Advisor to startups, SMBs and family-owned businesses
